claim: Fission yeast has three primary actin cytoskeleton networks: endocytic actin patches (assembled by Arp2/3 complex), polarizing actin cables (assembled by formin For3), and the cytokinetic contractile ring (assembled by formin Cdc12).
source: Fission yeast has three primary actin cytoskeleton networks, in which all of the actin filaments are assembled by a distinct actin assembly factor: endocytic actin patches (Arp2/3 complex), polarizing actin cables (formin For3), and the cytokinetic contractile ring (formin Cdc12).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a factual description of fission yeast actin networks and their assembly factors.

claim: Each of the three primary F-actin networks in fission yeast contains a distinct set of actin binding proteins (ABPs).
source: Moreover, each of these F-actin networks contains a distinct set of ABPs.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of fission yeast F-actin networks.

claim: Competition between tropomyosin Cdc8, fimbrin Fim1, and ADF/cofilin Adf1 results in the exclusion of tropomyosin from actin patches.
source: We previously discovered that competition between ABPs tropomyosin Cdc8, fimbrin Fim1, and ADF/cofilin Adf1 results in the exclusion of tropomyosin from actin patches (Skau and Kovar, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Tropomyosin is a two-chained, parallel coiled-coil composed of two polypeptide chains with a characteristic heptad-repeat of hydrophobic residues.
source: Tropomyosin is a two-chained, parallel coiled-coil composed of two polypeptide chains with a characteristic heptad-repeat of hydrophobic residues (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an established structural characteristic of tropomyosin, with reference to a figure showing the structure.

claim: Individual tropomyosin coiled coils associate end-to-end to form continuous tropomyosin cables that extend along both sides of the helical actin filament.
source: Individual tropomyosin coiled coils associate end-to-end to form continuous tropomyosin cables that extend along both sides of the helical actin filament (Hanson and Lowy, 1963; Skoumpla et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Vertebrate tropomyosins span six or seven actin subunits in the filament.
source: Vertebrate tropomyosins span six or seven actin subunits in the filament.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of vertebrate tropomyosins.

claim: The two S. cerevisiae tropomyosin isoforms span four or five actins.
source: Yeast tropomyosins are shorter: the two S. cerevisiae tropomyosin isoforms span four or five actins, while S. pombe tropomyosin Cdc8 (hereafter called Cdc8) spans four actin subunits.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of S. cerevisiae tropomyosins.

claim: S. pombe tropomyosin Cdc8 spans four actin subunits.
source: Yeast tropomyosins are shorter: the two S. cerevisiae tropomyosin isoforms span four or five actins, while S. pombe tropomyosin Cdc8 (hereafter called Cdc8) spans four actin subunits.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of S. pombe Cdc8.

claim: Fluorescently labeling tropomyosins is generally problematic as mutations or insertions within the protein can potentially disrupt its coiled-coil structure.
source: However, fluorescently labeling tropomyosins is generally problematic as mutations or insertions within the protein can potentially disrupt its coiled-coil structure (Greenfield and Hitchcock-DeGregori, 1995).
evidence: This is stated as a known challenge in tropomyosin labeling, supported by citation.

claim: Tropomyosins labeled on the N- or C-terminus are not fully functional, as the presence of a label blocks end-to-end associations between tropomyosin molecules.
source: Additionally, tropomyosins labeled on the N- or C-terminus are not fully functional, as the presence of a label blocks end-to-end associations between tropomyosin molecules (Brooker et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation of terminal labeling, supported by citation.

claim: Once an initial Cdc8 site was initiated, spreading of Cdc8 occurred toward both the barbed and pointed ends at similar rates (3.2 and 2.4 Cdc8 molecules sec−1 μM−1, respectively, p-value=0.037).
source: Once an initial Cdc8 site was initiated, spreading of Cdc8 occurred toward both the barbed and pointed ends at similar rates (3.2 and 2.4 Cdc8 molecules sec−1 μM−1, respectively, p-value=0.037).

claim: There was considerable variation in Cdc8 spreading rates in both directions, between ~1–6 Cdc8 molecules sec−1 μM−1.

claim: Two distinct Cdc8 cables loading on the same actin filament were observed by TIRFM.

claim: The observed binding of the second Cdc8 cable opposite a first Cdc8 cable was higher than what was predicted by a model of stochastic binding.

claim: Although initial Cdc8 molecules bind stochastically on the actin filament, there is a bias for subsequent Cdc8 molecules to bind opposite previously-established Cdc8 stretches, indicating a potential role for indirect cooperativity.

claim: A model with only end-to-end cooperativity produced a much lower fraction of F-actin doubly coated with Cdc8 compared to the experimental data.

claim: End-to-end cooperative binding alone does not fully account for the experimentally observed Cdc8 loading behavior.
